message.content:
In Christianity, there isn’t a single “official” ranking of prophets that applies uniformly across all denominations. Different traditions highlight different figures:

| Tradition | Emphasis |
|-----------|----------|
| **Catholic & Orthodox** | Jesus Christ is seen as the fulfillment of Old‑Testament prophecy; Moses, Isaiah, and John the Baptist are also highly revered. |
| **Protestant (especially evangelical)** | Jesus is central, with Moses and Paul often highlighted as foundational. |
| **Lutheran** | Jesus is the focal point, with the Old Testament prophets viewed as foreshadowing Him. |
| **Reformed** | Jesus is paramount, with the prophetic tradition seen as pointing toward His redemptive work. |

So while many Christians regard Jesus Christ as the most pivotal figure—often called the “Prophet” in the sense of being the one who fulfills the prophetic promises—the importance placed on other prophets varies widely.
